rendered:
According to the US Advanced Battery Consortium standards, an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life when its current cell capacity falls below 80%[1] of its rated capacity: "an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life when its current cell capacity is less than 80% of the rated capacity[2]"

Once it reaches that point, the end-of-life EV battery can be reused/repurposed, recycled, or disposed of in landfills, which the review notes would cause serious environmental issues. Repurposing reconfigures the batteries for a second life in applications such as grid energy storage and behind-the-meter energy storage.

The review says that, regardless of whether batteries are reused, they all eventually need to be recycled[3].
